html:
Diocletian's Palace is the fortified retirement palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian, built around 300 on the Dalmatian coast, and the old centre of the city of Split in Croatia.

Diocletian, born in Dalmatia, gave up the throne in 305, the first emperor to give up power by choice, and lived here until his death. His mausoleum is now the Cathedral of Saint Domnius, named after a bishop martyred in his persecution. In the 600s refugees from nearby Salona, sacked by Avars and Slavs, moved inside the walls, and the palace grew into a town. Houses, shops and churches still fill its halls. It is one of the best preserved Roman palaces anywhere and a World Heritage Site.
sum: Diocletian's Palace is the fortified retirement palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian, built around 300 on the Dalmatian coast, and the old centre of the city of Split in Croatia.
